question.text: When benzene sulphonic acid and $p$-nitrophenol are treated with $\mathrm{NaHCO}_3$, the gases released respectively are

solution.text:
$$ \text { Benzene sulphonic acid and p-nitrophenol react with } \mathrm{NaHCO}_3 \text { and evolve } \mathrm{CO}_2 \text { gas. } $$
Because benezene sulphonic acid and $p$-nitro phenol are stronger acids with $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{CO}_3$ (i.e., $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}+\mathrm{CO}_2$ ) so, they are capable to evolve $\mathrm{CO}_2$ with $\mathrm{NaHCO}_3$. $$ \mathrm{HCO}_3^{-}+\underset{\text { Acid }}{\mathrm{H}^{+}} \rightarrow \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}+\mathrm{CO}_2 \uparrow $$
